The search didn't turn up anything about the `--durable-objects-code-update-mode` flag itself. None of the results mention it, so I can't confirm whether it exists or what it does.

The results do cover how Wrangler deploys Durable Object code in general:

- **Code updates vs. migrations:** One Cloudflare doc says that editing an existing Durable Object class's code needs no migration, and that you update it by re-running `wrangler deploy` ([source](https://f75b423c.previews.developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/reference/durable-object-class-migrations-legacy/index.md)).
- **Lifecycle changes under gradual deployments:** Cloudflare's gradual deployment docs say that Worker bundles changing a Durable Object's class lifecycle (creating, renaming, or deleting classes) can't be uploaded as part of a gradual rollout. They recommend running `npx wrangler deploy` for these changes and keeping them separate from other code changes ([source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/versions-and-deployments/gradual-deployments/with-durable-objects/index.md)).
- **Version assignment:** Under gradual rollouts, each Durable Object instance is pinned to one Worker version at a time, since only one version of a given object can run at once ([source](https://codex-container-api-docs.previews.developers.cloudflare.com/workers/versions-and-deployments/gradual-deployments/with-durable-objects/)).

My suggestion is to check the Wrangler CLI reference or its changelog directly for that flag, since the search index didn't cover it.

The flag was added in **wrangler 4.141.0**, a minor release that the workers-sdk release notes list as "Add Durable Objects code update strategies to Worker deployments" (PR #15658). Immediate mode can be used with deploy, versions deploy, and rollback to push code without waiting for active Durable Object instances to hibernate.

Deferred mode accepts a maximum delay, such as 30s, and can also be set in config through durable_objects.code_update_strategy with mode and max_delay. If unset, the strategy defaults to deferred with a five-minute maximum delay, and delays are capped at 24 hours with millisecond precision.

The 4.141.0 commit list names the same PR as a "hibernation timeout option," so the title differs from the release note wording. The search also surfaced a newer release, wrangler 4.149.0 (October 8), but its results didn't mention this flag, so I couldn't confirm whether its behavior changed after 4.141.0.

content.text:
The flag controls when Durable Object instances that are already running switch to the new code you just deployed. It was added in wrangler 4.141.0 (PR #15658, "Add Durable Objects code update strategies to Worker deployments"), and it works with `wrangler deploy`, `wrangler versions deploy` and `wrangler rollback`.

- **Immediate mode** pushes the new code to active instances right away, without waiting for them to hibernate.
- **Deferred mode** is the default. It lets active instances keep running the old code for up to a maximum delay (for example `30s`), after which the update is applied. If you don't set anything, the delay is five minutes, and the maximum allowed is 24 hours.

You can also set this in your config file with `durable_objects.code_update_strategy`, using `mode` and `max_delay`.

I got this from release notes and search summaries rather than the CLI reference. Run `wrangler deploy --help` on your version to check the exact syntax. I also couldn't confirm whether anything changed after 4.141.0; the latest release I found was 4.149.0.

- [Gradual deployments with Durable Objects](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/versions-and-deployments/gradual-deployments/with-durable-objects/)
